## Player-facing intent and constraints

Make the existing hunter's warning display legible as an ecological signal during warn/investigate/pursue. Give the existing fins/eye highlights a bounded, slow brightness pulse and a clear difference from idle/disengage. Preserve the richer-cel palette and readable animal form. Prefer selective warm fin markings/eyes over washing out the entire body. This is a warning display, not a flashing UI target. A suggested starting range is roughly0.6–1 Hz and modest gain; select final values using actual before/after footage and report them. No fast strobe, new threat geometry/silhouette or extra invented creature behavior.

Keep every hunter pose, scale, fin/body animation transform, collision, warning/attack timing, territory, speed, damage, noise and distraction response unchanged. Preserve pause behavior: pulse time follows existing simulation time and does not advance while paused. Reset correctly on null/scene rebuild/state replacement. Same geometry remains attached to the same actor and authored eyes/fins. No marker, outline or silhouette through walls; ordinary opaque depth tests, cel lighting and current optical fog apply to the entire display.

Use the existing scene-owned cel material and existing emissive vertex-color convention (`ArtBatch.glow` / alpha), with retained per-mesh buffers or equivalent bounded render-only data. Do not change shared material uniforms/shaders or brighten other meshes. Avoid creating meshes/materials/buffers every frame. If separating existing eye or fin color groups is necessary, preserve their exact world geometry and keep the additional draw/memory count explicit. Prefer reuse and selected color updates. Do not change the water, camera, aperture, terrain or actor bounds to improve a shot.

Actual deep fog may still obscure the hunter at long range. Report that limit precisely rather than bypassing fog or moving the animal/player. The later sound-bearing cue is complementary. Do not claim an on-screen or unobstructed animal is necessarily human-readable. A diagnostic may report actual camera distance, frustum, LOS, estimated attenuation/projected size, but use the real camera/optics and label estimates; keep diagnostics out of shipped UI/source unless a reusable test truly requires them.
